title: C#: from the first program to reliable .NET applications
summary: 48 detailed lessons from first programs through language mechanisms, reliable systems and independently designed projects.

lessons.title: Source, compilation and the first observable result
lessons.outcome: Model boxes containing packets containing items. Explain each intermediate value and check the final product.
lessons.lab: Write a program calculating the number of seats in four rows of six seats. Check 24 explicitly.
lessons.verification: Hello, C# appears before the lesson marker. The total is 12, while adding the two inputs gives 7.

lessons.title: Types, variables and explicit conversions
lessons.outcome: Design an input boundary for a percentage and document its accepted textual and numeric ranges.
lessons.lab: Write a TryParse-based validator accepting only nonnegative whole-number quantities.
lessons.verification: The integer result is 3 and the floating result is 3.5. 42 parses successfully; words fail without an exception.

lessons.title: Numeric range, checked overflow and decimal amounts
lessons.outcome: Design a quantity and currency contract that states overflow, rounding and invalid-input behavior.
lessons.lab: Calculate a decimal subtotal and tax, rounding only the final payable amount.
lessons.verification: The maximum int plus one is rejected; 100 plus 20 is accepted. Two valid midpoint policies produce 2.34 and 2.35.

lessons.title: Strings, interpolation and Unicode text
lessons.outcome: Design a text-field limit and explain whether its contract measures bytes, scalars or user-visible graphemes.
lessons.lab: Implement case-insensitive machine-key comparison with an explicit policy.
lessons.verification: The original remains data while the result is DATA. One scalar occupies two UTF-16 units and four UTF-8 bytes.

lessons.title: Boolean decisions and exhaustive alternatives
lessons.outcome: Choose a routing policy with three mutually exclusive outcomes and explain how invalid values are represented.
lessons.lab: Write a classifier for negative, zero and positive temperatures.
lessons.verification: The missing value is handled without dereferencing null. 59 retries, 60 passes, and 101 is rejected.

lessons.title: Loops, invariants and termination
lessons.outcome: Design a bounded retry loop and explain both its invariant and its stopping argument.
lessons.lab: Implement a first-match search returning a separate not-found representation.
lessons.verification: The sum is 12 and the empty sum is zero. The first 8 is at index 1; 9 is absent.

lessons.title: Methods, parameters and return contracts
lessons.outcome: Extract one computation from a larger program and state its input, output, mutation and failure contract.
lessons.lab: Write a method computing an area from validated nonnegative dimensions.
lessons.verification: The result is 14 and the caller still holds 7. 12 divided by 3 returns 4; the exact-integer contract rejects 7 divided by 2.

lessons.title: Arrays, indices and rectangular data
lessons.outcome: Choose rectangular or jagged storage for variable-length sensor histories and justify the choice.
lessons.lab: Compute each row sum of the two-by-three grid.
lessons.verification: The alias changes source; the copied integer array retains 2. The shape is two by three and the sum is 21.

lessons.title: Lists, capacity and safe mutation
lessons.outcome: Choose mutation or a new sequence for an undoable editor operation and explain who observes the change.
lessons.lab: Produce a filtered list while preserving the original.
lessons.verification: Reserving ten slots leaves Count at zero; two appends produce Count two. Two entries are removed while the earlier integer snapshot keeps four values.

lessons.title: Dictionaries, sets and identity policies
lessons.outcome: Design stable identity for records and explain which fields may change without invalidating lookup.
lessons.lab: Build a frequency dictionary from a list of tags.
lessons.verification: OAK finds a present zero; Pine is absent. RED is a duplicate under the selected comparer.

lessons.title: Nullability and optional information
lessons.outcome: Design an import field whose missing value has different meaning from an explicit zero or empty value.
lessons.lab: Write a formatter preserving missing, zero and positive measurements.
lessons.verification: The optional length is absent, not zero. A measured zero and an unknown measurement produce distinct descriptions.

lessons.title: Value copies, references and mutation ownership
lessons.outcome: Design a data boundary that prevents callers from mutating an internal collection.
lessons.lab: Choose a representation for a coordinate and for a shared session, explaining the difference.
lessons.verification: Changing the copied point leaves the original X at 2. Both references observe the same counter increment.

lessons.title: Classes, constructors and encapsulated invariants
lessons.outcome: Explain whether a shared wallet needs synchronization when several tasks may spend concurrently.
lessons.lab: Implement a bounded inventory whose reservations never make stock negative.
lessons.verification: Spending 4 succeeds; spending 7 afterward fails without changing 6. Negative spending is rejected and zero is an accepted no-op.

lessons.title: Records, structs and data equality
lessons.outcome: Choose identity-based or data-based equality for an order and explain how updates affect collection membership.
lessons.lab: Design an immutable coordinate using a readonly record struct.
lessons.verification: Equal records can be distinct objects; with preserves the previous age. Both records see the appended list item.

lessons.title: Patterns and explicit state models
lessons.outcome: Replace several loosely related flags in a program with explicit states and justify which impossible combinations disappear.
lessons.lab: Model a loading, ready and failed operation with separate payloads.
lessons.verification: The same method distinguishes type, value range and string shape. Success carries a count; failure carries a reason.

lessons.title: Foundation project: a validated inventory report
lessons.outcome: Design a reusable import result that retains per-line rejection reasons without exposing sensitive raw input.
lessons.lab: Build a sorted text report from the accepted dictionary and the rejection count.
lessons.verification: Pear totals 6 and apple totals 3. Three rejected lines do not alter the valid pear total.

lessons.title: Interfaces and substitutable behavior
lessons.outcome: Choose one dependency worth injecting in the inventory importer and explain the testing benefit.
lessons.lab: Define a small interface for a deterministic label formatter.
lessons.verification: Four units cost 12 and zero units cost zero. The same consumer applies a capped or uncapped policy.

lessons.title: Generics and constraints that express capabilities
lessons.outcome: Design a generic helper with the smallest useful capability constraint.
lessons.lab: Create a generic immutable three-element container.
lessons.verification: The same method returns an int or a string without object casts. Swap preserves the element type, and a tie remains a valid value.

lessons.title: Delegates, closures and events
lessons.outcome: Design ownership for subscriptions in a screen or service that can be disposed.
lessons.lab: Write a transformation method accepting Func<int,int>.
lessons.verification: Changing factor changes later calls through the closure. Only the first emission reaches the removed handler.

lessons.title: LINQ, deferred execution and materialization
lessons.outcome: Choose streaming or materialization for a large import and explain memory and repeatability tradeoffs.
lessons.lab: Build a deterministic report selecting, transforming and ordering records.
lessons.verification: The deferred query sees the subsequently appended 3. The earlier snapshot contains only 2 while a new projection sees three values.

lessons.title: Grouping, joins and data grain
lessons.outcome: Design checks that distinguish one-to-one, one-to-many and many-to-many joins before aggregation.
lessons.lab: Build a report joining unique item metadata to item totals.
lessons.verification: Three event rows become two category totals. One left row becomes two joined rows.

lessons.title: Iterators and lazy sequence contracts
lessons.outcome: Choose a sequence API for a large file and document repeated-enumeration and resource-lifetime behavior.
lessons.lab: Implement a lazy sequence of cumulative totals.
lessons.verification: The consumer receives 5 and 6 and can stop before the full range. Negative count is rejected immediately, without enumeration.

lessons.title: Exceptions and preserving failure meaning
lessons.outcome: Decide which layer owns user-facing error translation and which details should remain private diagnostics.
lessons.lab: Define an import API with distinct invalid-input and storage-failure outcomes.
lessons.verification: Malformed numeric text is caught as a format error. The outer domain failure still contains the I/O cause.

lessons.title: Disposable resources and deterministic cleanup
lessons.outcome: Document ownership and leave-open behavior for a parser that wraps a stream reader.
lessons.lab: Write a helper that reads from a caller-owned stream without closing it.
lessons.verification: The resource is open inside and closed afterward. The controlled exception still triggers cleanup.

lessons.title: Files, paths and local data ownership
lessons.outcome: Explain what must change to make a persistent report update crash-recoverable.
lessons.lab: Build a temporary-file round trip for a small inventory report.
lessons.verification: The Unicode text round-trips and the owned directory is removed. A simple leaf name and a nested path are recognized as different shapes.

lessons.title: JSON contracts and schema evolution
lessons.outcome: Design a migration from a renamed quantity field while retaining old saved records.
lessons.lab: Write a decoder returning explicit validation errors for missing name and negative quantity.
lessons.verification: The restored name and quantity match the original record. Valid JSON can decode into a rejected domain value.

lessons.title: Dates, durations and culture-independent data
lessons.outcome: Design storage and display policies for appointments in a named time zone.
lessons.lab: Build a duration report using fixed UTC timestamps.
lessons.verification: The values denote the same instant despite different offsets. The elapsed duration is 90 minutes and the timestamp round-trips.

lessons.title: Testing contracts with meaningful counterexamples
lessons.outcome: Separate unit and integration evidence for a JSON file importer.
lessons.lab: Write table-driven checks for your inventory quantity validator.
lessons.verification: Negative, zero and positive cases preserve their intended categories. The zero case catches the incorrect default, and clamping twice changes nothing further.

lessons.title: Async, await and task completion
lessons.outcome: Explain when CPU work might need scheduling separately from an asynchronous I/O API.
lessons.lab: Write an async method returning a validated total.
lessons.verification: Await yields 7 and confirms successful completion. WhenAll retains input order and await exposes the task exception.

lessons.title: Cooperative cancellation and bounded waiting
lessons.outcome: Design an operation receipt distinguishing cancelled waiting, confirmed cancellation and unknown outcome.
lessons.lab: Write an operation that stops cooperatively and preserves already committed work.
lessons.verification: The token check acknowledges cancellation. The wait cancels, then the original task later completes with 9.

lessons.title: Bounded channels and producer-consumer ownership
lessons.outcome: Choose wait, reject or drop behavior for a workload and explain what evidence the producer receives.
lessons.lab: Build a bounded producer-consumer pipeline with explicit writer completion.
lessons.verification: The first item is accepted and the second immediate write is refused. Both admitted items are read after completion, and later writes fail.

lessons.title: Composition project: a deterministic import service
lessons.outcome: Design an adapter boundary for a file or HTTP source without putting I/O inside the pure aggregation.
lessons.lab: Build a per-item result while preserving the rejected count.
lessons.verification: The service returns total 2 and one rejected record. A cancelled request and a successful empty import have different outcomes.

lessons.title: Threads, locks and compound invariants
lessons.outcome: Choose immutable snapshots or a lock for a shared report cache and justify the ownership model.
lessons.lab: Implement a locked transfer preserving the sum of two balances.
lessons.verification: Four tasks produce exactly 400 increments. The reader uses the same gate as mutation.

lessons.title: Atomic operations and concurrent collections
lessons.outcome: Explain why atomically updating two separate balances does not preserve a transfer invariant.
lessons.lab: Build a concurrent frequency counter using pure update functions.
lessons.verification: The atomic count is exactly 400. Twenty admitted updates produce 20.

lessons.title: Span, slices and memory lifetime
lessons.outcome: Choose Span or Memory for a synchronous parser and an asynchronous buffer owner.
lessons.lab: Write a synchronous span helper counting separators.
lessons.verification: Only the middle element changes. The digit total is 6 and empty input totals zero.

lessons.title: Garbage collection, pooling and retained memory
lessons.outcome: Decide whether pooling is justified using allocation measurements and a stated lifetime contract.
lessons.lab: Write a pooled-buffer helper with finally-based return.
lessons.verification: Only three initialized elements contribute to the total. Clearing removes the application references without promising collection timing.

lessons.title: Algorithmic complexity and measured performance
lessons.outcome: Write a benchmark plan specifying workload, correctness checks, warmup and allocation measurements.
lessons.lab: Compare repeated list scans with one built index while preserving equality policy.
lessons.verification: Finding the last element needs four comparisons. The index answers membership while storing four identities.

lessons.title: Validation, regular expressions and bounded input
lessons.outcome: Choose a parser or regex for a nested format and justify complexity and error reporting.
lessons.lab: Validate a structured identifier and then check its domain-specific reserved words.
lessons.verification: The identifier begins with a lowercase letter and uses only admitted characters. The plus sign is matched literally.

lessons.title: HTTP clients, status contracts and offline transport tests
lessons.outcome: Design a retry policy that distinguishes safe reads from writes with unknown outcomes.
lessons.lab: Write a client method accepting a supplied HttpClient and CancellationToken.
lessons.verification: The handler supplies count 3 without network access. 503 remains an observable failure rather than a default successful count.

lessons.title: Domain architecture and dependency direction
lessons.outcome: Draw dependency direction for a command-line adapter, HTTP adapter and shared domain library.
lessons.lab: Extract the inventory aggregation into a transport-independent core.
lessons.verification: The result uses the supplied instant. A different clock does not bypass identity validation.

lessons.title: API design and the prepared ASP.NET project
lessons.outcome: Design idempotent update behavior and explain how duplicate creation differs.
lessons.lab: Run the separately prepared ApiLab project and inspect GET and POST responses.
lessons.verification: Valid input maps to the created outcome. Invalid requests produce 400 decisions.

lessons.title: Security boundaries, secrets and untrusted data
lessons.outcome: Describe authorization checks for a resource owned by another user and the evidence each check needs.
lessons.lab: Design an allowlist of fields safe to include in an import error.
lessons.verification: Read is allowed and delete is denied. The token is replaced while a status remains visible.

lessons.title: Projects, packages and reproducible builds
lessons.outcome: Design a dependency update review including lock changes, license checks and runtime evidence.
lessons.lab: Move a pure domain type into the supplied class-library project and run its executable checks.
lessons.verification: The running framework generation is compatible with the declared classroom target. The example preserves the intended target and nullable policy.

lessons.title: Diagnostics, structured events and operational evidence
lessons.outcome: Design a latency report that includes percentiles, sample count and measurement boundaries.
lessons.lab: Instrument your import project with submitted, accepted and rejected counts.
lessons.verification: The serialized event contains an explicit rejected outcome. Five submitted records are fully accounted for and rejection rate is 0.4.

lessons.title: Reflection, native boundaries and AOT tradeoffs
lessons.outcome: Plan an external Native AOT experiment stating target architecture, native prerequisites and runtime checks.
lessons.lab: Replace string-based access in a small report with a typed projection.
lessons.verification: The known property is an int and the missing property is absent. The fixed projection needs no string-based member lookup.

lessons.title: Modern C# features and version-aware readability
lessons.outcome: Review a proposed new feature and justify adopting it using readability, compatibility and tooling evidence.
lessons.lab: Refactor one simple class to a primary constructor without changing behavior.
lessons.verification: The target types select array and list representations. The supplied factor is used by the instance operation.

lessons.title: Resilience, idempotency and unknown outcomes
lessons.outcome: Design durable atomic storage for an effect and its receipt and state remaining failure modes.
lessons.lab: Implement a result lookup that does not execute the command again.
lessons.verification: The repeated identity returns its prior result without increasing the total. A new identity applies separately, while a changed payload under an old key is rejected.

lessons.title: Capstone: a reviewable .NET data application
lessons.outcome: Deliver a project README with build commands, architecture, failure policies, tests, operational limits and a proposed next extension.
lessons.lab: Build the external DomainLab and expose the domain contract through the ApiLab adapter.
lessons.verification: The sorted report is a=3;b=6. A valid zero remains in the report while two invalid rows are counted.
